query: meta-agent modifies training environment during multi-turn reinforcement learning
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16523v1)** (October 2026) — The closest match: a meta-agent monitors multi-turn RL training and modifies the environment, user simulator, rewards, and training configuration. Validated changes are applied during ongoing runs. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher); Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).

2. **[Weak-for-Strong: Training Weak Meta-Agent to Harness Strong Executors](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04785v1)** (April 2025) — Related work using multi-turn RL to train a smaller meta-agent to iteratively design and improve workflows for stronger models. Its focus is workflow optimization rather than live training-environment modification. **People:** Fan Nie, Haotian Ye, Weixin Liang, Pan Lu, and James Zou (Stanford University); Lan Feng and Alexandre Alahi (EPFL); Huaxiu Yao (UNC–Chapel Hill).

1. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://lifelongagent.github.io/Project-Lifelong-Agent/UserRL/index.html)** — Directly relevant to reward design: studies how turn-level rewards and whole-conversation scoring affect agents trained against simulated users. **People:** Cheng Qian and Heng Ji (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, and colleagues (Salesforce AI Research).

Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy, and Yoon Kim. **Affiliations:** MIT, Stanford University, and MIT–IBM Watson AI Lab.

query: within-run and across-run adaptation agent training
text:

   **People:** Wenxiao Zhao, Dong Liu, Kaiyi Xu, Feng Liu, Zhen Zhao, and colleagues. **Affiliations:** Shanghai AI Laboratory, UCLA, and Tongji University.

2. **[CoWork-X: Experience-Optimized Co-Evolution for Multi-Agent Collaboration System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05004)** (2026) — Combines fast coordination within episodes with post-episode learning: an optimizer reviews execution logs and updates a reusable skill library.  
   **People:** Zexin Lin, Jiachen Yu, Haoyang Zhang, Yuzhao Li, Zhonghang Li, Yujiu Yang, Junjie Wang, and Xiaoqiang Ji. **Affiliations:** CUHK Shenzhen, Tsinghua University, AutoGame Research, and Shenzhen Institute of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics for Society.

3. **[Hyperagents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461)** (2026) — Agents modify both their task-solving code and their improvement mechanisms; the paper reports improvements that transfer across domains and accumulate across runs.

query: multi-turn reinforcement learning user simulation benchmarks
text:
1. **[LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models](https://lmrl-gym.github.io/)** — A direct match: eight dialogue and text-game tasks with online simulators and offline training datasets. **People:** Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, Yuexiang Zhai (UC Berkeley); Kelvin Xu (Google DeepMind); Sergey Levine (UC Berkeley and Google DeepMind).

2. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.19736v1)** — Standardized environments pairing agents with simulated users for multi-turn RL training and evaluation. **People:** Cheng Qian (Salesforce AI Research and UIUC), Heng Ji (UIUC), and Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Zhiwei Liu, Haolin Chen, Shirley Kokane, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Huan Wang (Salesforce AI Research).

3. **[τ²-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.07982v1)** — Tests interactions where both the agent and simulated user can operate tools and change a shared environment. **People:** Victor Barres, Soham Ray, Karthik Narasimhan (Sierra); Honghua Dong (Sierra, University of Toronto, Vector Institute); Xujie Si (University of Toronto and Vector Institute).

4. **[MUA-RL: Multi-turn User-interacting Agent Reinforcement Learning for Agentic Tool Use](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18669v1)** — Integrates simulated users into RL training; evaluates on τ-bench, τ²-Bench, BFCL-V3 Multi Turn, and ACEBench. **People:** Weikang Zhao (Meituan and Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences); Xili Wang (Meituan and Peking University); Chengdi Ma (Peking University); Lingbin Kong, Zhaohua Yang, Mingxiang Tuo, Xiaowei Shi, Yitao Zhai, Xunliang Cai (Meituan).

5. **[UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.38043v1)** — Evaluates whether simulated users follow their assigned instructions, independently of agent success; particularly relevant to simulator reliability in RL. **People:** Ashish Jain and Armaan Sandhu. The paper’s HTML does not explicitly state institutional affiliations.

query: methods improving user-centric agents with simulated users
text:
1. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.19736v1)** (2025). Trains agents through simulated-user interactions, studying reward shaping and conversation-level scoring to improve effectiveness and efficiency. **People:** Cheng Qian (Salesforce AI Research and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign), Heng Ji (UIUC), Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, and colleagues (Salesforce AI Research).

2. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16523v1)** (2026). Uses a meta-agent to diagnose training problems and jointly improve user simulators, environments, rewards, and agent training settings. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta), Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore), Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology), Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher), and Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).

3. **[Training Proactive and Personalized LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.02208v1)** (2025). Introduces **UserVille**, with preference-aware simulated users, and **PPP**, reinforcement learning that rewards task completion, useful clarification questions, and personalization. **People:** Weiwei Sun, Xuhui Zhou, Weihua Du, and colleagues (Carnegie Mellon University), with Xingyao Wang (OpenHands).

4. **[MIMESIS: Learning User Simulators as Training Environments for Interactive Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.09484v1)** (2026). Learns realistic user behavior from human conversations, then improves agents through simulated interactions and coaching derived from simulator feedback. **People:** Hoang Phan (Meta Superintelligence Labs and New York University), Dat Huynh and Deren Lei (Meta Superintelligence Labs), Changdae Oh (Meta and University of Wisconsin–Madison), and colleagues.
